items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-07-21
items.q: Andy Kirk with Claude Zajore. I'm trying to think of a piano player. Boy, the guy was fastest right hand I've ever seen in my life, I heard.

ctx.x: Was that about why you bought the Zoot Suit?

Well, yes, because it was a style at the time. John McNeely, Charles Dimes, myself, Edward Johnson, we were all good friends. And we all would meet down on Rampart Street and we'd party at the Pelican or sometime we went to the Tick Tock. We used to go to the, see, then we'd go to the Palace Theater where all the big bands would come. And we had Savannah Churchill, where Red Fox, where, let's see who all would come down there. I'm just trying to think of one of them. Buddy Johnson played down there. Favorite…
So, what was, when you talked about Rampart Street, was that like the happening?

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: I'm thinking about this man here, Andy Kirk and it's Clouds of Joy. And you talk about a band. Wow, boy. You know, I still have some of those recordings.

ctx.x: Woody Herman. My God, it's a who's who.

That's right. That's a collector's item. In other words, Ted, you and me are sitting down here talking about history, the way it was and the way it should be. And for some particular reason, you still at that time had an element of people did not want to see progress between blacks and whites. You know, when I think back, had it not been for Louis Messina, there would not have been whites and blacks fighting against each other at the Coliseum Arena.
